# Base R Charts

## Bar chart
```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=7}
frequencies <- c(Female = 35, Children = 25, Male = 40)
barplot(frequencies, cex.names = 0.8,
        names.arg = names(frequencies),
        col = c("purple", "salmon", "pink"))
```
`cex.names` shrinks the axis labels; lower it further if labels get cut off.

## Pie chart
```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=8}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
pie(frequencies, cex = 0.8,
    labels = paste0(names(frequencies), " (", frequencies, ")"),
    col = c("purple", "salmon", "pink"))
pie(frequencies, cex = 0.8,
    labels = paste0(names(frequencies), " (", frequencies, ")"),
    col = rainbow(length(frequencies)))
```

## Histograms and density
```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=8}
set.seed(12092024)
x <- sample(1:120, size = 1000, replace = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
hist(x, probability = TRUE) # densities instead of raw counts
plot(density(x), col = "salmon", main = "density of x")
```

```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=6}
with(iris, hist(Sepal.Length, probability = TRUE))
lines(density(iris$Sepal.Length), col = "red")
```

## Scatter plot
```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=6}
x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 50)
y <- sin(x)
plot(x, y, pch = 16, col = "blue")
```

**Exercise:** scatter plot of `Petal.Length` vs `Petal.Width`, colored by
species, with a fitted regression line.
```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=6}
f <- Petal.Length ~ Petal.Width
lr <- lm(f, data = iris)
plot(f, data = iris, col = iris$Species, pch = 16)
abline(lr, col = "blue", lwd = 2, lty = 3)
legend("topleft", legend = unique(iris$Species),
       col = unique(iris$Species), pch = 16, bty = "n")
```

# Distribution Simulations

## Uniform distribution

$$
f_X(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{1}{b-a} & \text{if } x \in[a, b] \\
0 & \text{else}\end{cases}
$$

```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=6}
set.seed(123)
x <- runif(1000)
hist(x, probability = TRUE, xlab = NULL,
     main = "Histogram of a uniform distribution", col = "turquoise")
lines(density(x), col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 3)
abline(v = mean(x), col = "blue", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
legend("topleft", lty = c(2, 2), col = c("red", "blue"),
       legend = c("Density", "Average"))
```

Testing whether a sample looks uniform vs. normal:
```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=5}
ks.test(x, "punif") # p > 0.05 supports "looks uniform"
qqnorm(x)
qqline(x, col = "red")
```

## Binomial distribution

$$
P(X = k) = {n \choose k}p^k(1-p)^{n-k}
$$

```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=8}
rbinom_dist <- rbinom(n = 10000, size = 1, prob = 0.3)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
pie(table(rbinom_dist))
barplot(table(rbinom_dist))
```
A histogram isn't well suited to discrete data like this — bar/pie charts
work better.

## Gaussian (normal) distribution

$$
f_X(x) = \frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}(x-\mu)^2\right\}
$$

```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=6}
set.seed(13092024)
gauss_dist <- rnorm(1000, mean = 0, sd = 1)
hist(gauss_dist, probability = TRUE, breaks = 30, xlab = NULL,
     main = "Histogram of a standard normal distribution", col = "turquoise")
lines(density(gauss_dist), col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
abline(v = mean(gauss_dist), col = "blue", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
```

```{r}
mean(gauss_dist)
sd(gauss_dist)
```

## Simulating a linear relationship

$$y_i = \alpha + \beta x_i + \varepsilon_i,\quad \varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1)$$

```{r}
set.seed(123)
x <- rnorm(1000, mean = 5, sd = 1.5)
error_term <- rnorm(1000)
z <- 4 + 8 * x + error_term # true relationship, known only because we simulated it

df <- data.frame(x, z)
head(df, 5)
```

Fitting a simple linear model:
```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=7}
LR <- lm(z ~ x, data = df)
coefs <- coefficients(LR)
summary(LR)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(LR) # standard diagnostic plots
```

Estimated model: $\hat{y} =$ `r round(coefs[[1]], 2)` + `r round(coefs[[2]], 2)`
$x$. Predicting for a new value, $x = 15$:
```{r}
new_data <- data.frame(x = 15)
(new_data$predicted <- predict(object = LR, newdata = new_data))
```

```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=6}
plot(predicted ~ x, data = new_data, col = "darkgreen", xlim = c(0, 15),
     ylim = c(0, new_data$predicted), pch = 16, ylab = "z")
points(z ~ x, data = df, col = "darkorange", pch = 20)
abline(LR, col = "blue")
legend("topleft", c("Actual", "Predicted"),
       col = c("darkorange", "darkgreen"), pch = c(20, 16), bty = "n")
```

## Exponential distribution
```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=6}
set.seed(13092024)
exp_dist <- rexp(1000, rate = 1)
hist(exp_dist, probability = TRUE, xlab = NULL,
     main = "Histogram of exponential distribution", col = "turquoise")
lines(density(exp_dist), col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
abline(v = mean(exp_dist), col = "blue", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
```

## Poisson distribution
```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=6}
set.seed(13092024)
pois_dist <- rpois(1000, lambda = 2.5)
hist(pois_dist, probability = TRUE, main = "Histogram of Poisson distribution",
     col = "turquoise", xlab = NULL)
lines(density(pois_dist), col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
abline(v = mean(pois_dist), col = "blue", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
```
